raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`_get_fused_hc_post_pre_buffers` caches one set of `mhc_post_pre` buffers per distinct `num_tokens` and never evicts them. The cache was added together with the `num_tokens <= _FUSED_HC_POST_PRE_M_THRESHOLD` (64) gate in #26383, so it stayed small. Since #36871, gfx1250 runs the Triton fused post+pre for every batch size, so each distinct prefill size adds a set that is never freed. For DeepSeek-V4-Pro (hidden 7168, `hc_mult` 4), one set is about 160 KB per token, or about 330 MB at 2048 tokens; over half of that is the fp32 `acc_partial`.

On gfx1250, a DeepSeek-V4-Pro prefill server (TP4, `--chunked-prefill-size 2048`) running a multi-turn agentic workload kept growing until it hit `torch.OutOfMemoryError` about an hour in. Live-tensor scans showed a growing set of `(896, M, 24)` fp32 buffers, one for each distinct M.

## Modifications

- Cache buffers only for `num_tokens <= _FUSED_HC_POST_PRE_M_THRESHOLD`, the bound the cache was designed for. The bound applies to every caller.
- Larger calls allocate their buffers per call; they go back to the caching allocator after use. Small (decode) batches keep using cached buffers.
- Today only gfx1250 runs this path above the threshold, so that is the only place behavior changes:
  - gfx95 enters it only for up to 64 tokens, when the aiter HIP kernel declines;
  - GLM-5-Next calls the boundary only for up to 16 tokens;
  - other platforms never reach it.
- Add a CPU regression test, `TestAmdFusedMhcBufferCache`. It fails on main (sizes 65 and 2048 stay cached) and passes with this change.

## Accuracy Tests

Outputs are not expected to change. The kernel and the buffer shapes are the same; for `num_tokens > 64` the buffers are just no longer reused across calls.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not benchmarked separately. Calls above 64 tokens make six extra caching-allocator allocations, and small batches are still served from the cache.

End-to-end memory on gfx1250: DeepSeek-V4-Pro, PD disaggregation 1P (TP4) + 1D (TP4), multi-turn agentic benchmark at concurrency 64, `--mem-fraction-static 0.82`. The run used a downstream build whose `deepseek_v4_fused_mhc.py` matches main, with an env-gated variant of this change that caches up to 512 tokens.

| Prefill server | TP0 `torch.cuda.memory_allocated` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| main | 427 GiB at failure (432 GiB device) | OOM about 58 min into the benchmark |
| bounded cache | 362.6 GiB -> 363.0 GiB over 2 h 11 min | benchmark completed (3,042 requests, 0 errors) |

cc @inkcherry 

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch:
@@ -170,7 +170,10 @@ def _get_fused_hc_post_pre_buffers(
             num_ksplit, num_tokens, dtype=torch.float32, device=device
         ),
     }
-    _FUSED_HC_POST_PRE_CACHE[key] = bufs
+    # Cache only small batches: a caller that runs this path for every prefill
+    # size (gfx1250) would otherwise keep one buffer set per num_tokens forever.
+    if num_tokens <= _FUSED_HC_POST_PRE_M_THRESHOLD:
+        _FUSED_HC_POST_PRE_CACHE[key] = bufs
     return bufs

@@ -1,10 +1,13 @@
 import unittest
 from unittest import mock
 
+import torch
+
 from sglang.srt.environ import envs
 from sglang.srt.models.deepseek_common.amd import deepseek_v4_fused_mhc
 from sglang.srt.runtime_context import override_platform
 from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
 
 register_cpu_ci(est_time=11, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
 
@@ -322,6 +325,33 @@ class _StopForward(Exception):
         layer.input_layernorm.assert_called_once_with(fused_hs)
 
 
+class TestAmdFusedMhcBufferCache(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_cache_keeps_only_decode_sized_batches(self):
+        """Only batches up to the M threshold may stay cached; larger ones are
+        allocated per call, or every distinct prefill size stays alive forever."""
+        threshold = deepseek_v4_fused_mhc._FUSED_HC_POST_PRE_M_THRESHOLD
+        fake_ops = (None, lambda *args, **kwargs: ({"BLOCK_K": 64}, False))
+        cache = deepseek_v4_fused_mhc._FUSED_HC_POST_PRE_CACHE
+        with (
+            mock.patch.object(
+                deepseek_v4_fused_mhc,
+                "_get_triton_mhc_post_pre_ops",
+                return_value=fake_ops,
+            ),
+            mock.patch.dict(cache, clear=True),
+        ):
+            for num_tokens in (1, threshold, threshold + 1, 2048):
+                bufs = deepseek_v4_fused_mhc._get_fused_hc_post_pre_buffers(
+                    num_tokens=num_tokens,
+                    hidden_size=64,
+                    hc_mult=4,
+                    dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+                    device=torch.device("cpu"),
+                )
+                self.assertIsNotNone(bufs)
+            self.assertEqual(sorted(key[0] for key in cache), [1, threshold])
+
+
 def _hardware_available() -> bool:
     try:
